text: In our culture. <break time="0.8s" /> The scientific method has more than any other. <break time="0.8s" /> Served as the base for contemporary professional practice. <break time="0.8s" /> The hypothetico deductive mode of inquiry. <break time="0.8s" /> As the instrument of professional knowledge growth. <break time="0.8s" /> Has evoked the compelling authority of reason, logic, and certainty. <break time="0.8s" /> As a bedrock foundation for professional practice. <break time="0.8s" /> But a careful examination indicates. <break time="0.8s" /> That rather than asserting. <break time="0.8s" /> That the world is perfectly reasonable, perfectly logical, or perfectly certain. <break time="0.8s" /> What is really highlighted by science. <break time="0.8s" /> Is that the world is open, uncertain. <break time="0.8s" /> And our knowledge of it is never final. <break time="0.8s" /> Scientific explanations are partial, conditional, approximate, indeterminate. <break time="0.8s" /> Inconclusive, uncertain, intermediate, and limited. <break time="0.8s" /> Hardly a bedrock foundation. <break time="0.8s" /> But more accurately an ambiguous, conditional one. <break time="0.8s" /> This is not to argue. <break time="0.8s" /> That the world is nothing but chaos. <break time="0.8s" /> But it does suggest. <break time="0.8s" /> That the notion. <break time="0.8s" /> That science is the path to certainty and eternal truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Is unwise. <break time="0.8s" /> In terms of our knowledge action problem. <break time="0.8s" /> This perception of science as ambiguous and conditional. <break time="0.8s" /> Is part of the bedrock foundation of the gap in understanding.
